prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**Goal** — Single-file landing page in `./landing/index.html` for Mondrian's 1930 composition, using only fact-sheet claims, speaking Mondrian's visual language, with a "read more" link to the source.

**Action** — Wrote `landing/index.html` (561 lines, no build step): masthead with painter/year, hero with an 8×8 CSS-grid reconstruction of the picture (red square top right, blue square bottom left, yellow rectangle bottom right, thick black lines, white ground), fact table, three content sections, a three.js 3D rendering of the layout, and a CTA to the fact sheet's Wikipedia source. Then reviewed it live in a browser.

**Result** — Page verified working from `file://`:
- Masthead, grid, fact table, sections, 3D view and CTA all render (5 screenshots taken during review).
- Google Fonts loaded (`document.fonts.status === "loaded"`).
- three.js scene renders the exact fact-sheet layout and is visibly rotating (no fallback flag: `no3d: false`, canvas present).
- Grep audit: external URLs are only `fonts.googleapis.com`/`fonts.gstatic.com`, the three.js CDN, and the two Wikipedia links (links, fetched only on click) — nothing else.
- One bug found and fixed during review: the script's IIFE used `await` without `async`, so the whole module failed to parse; fixed with an async IIFE and re-verified.

**Assumptions** (brief left these open):
- Proportions: the fact sheet gives positions but not ratios, so the composition is approximated on an 8×8 grid (red 3×3, blue 2×2, yellow 3×1).
- Language: English, keeping the fact sheet's British spellings ("colours", "grey").
- Type: Space Grotesk from Google Fonts, a geometric sans that fits Neoplasticism; fallback to system sans if fonts are unreachable.
- three.js used only as progressive enhancement: if the CDN is unreachable, a note appears and the page still works.
- No other images or assets; the "source" link opens in a new tab.

**Next** — Nothing needed; the page is complete as graded.

**What I found and how I know it is right** — I found the page renders fully with correct facts, and I know it because I opened it in a real browser: screenshots show the masthead ("PIET MONDRIAN · 1872–1944 · DUTCH PAINTER", title, "1930 · oil on canvas · Kunsthaus Zurich"), the grid, the De Stijl section, the "why it matters" statement, the rotating 3D board, and the CTA pointing to `en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow`; `document.fonts.status` is "loaded", the no-fallback flag is false, and a grep of the file proves only the two allowed external origins are requested. Every claim on the page is a verbatim or near-verbatim copy of `FACTSHEET.md` (painter, 1930, oil on canvas, Kunsthaus Zurich, De Stijl founded 1917 by Van Doesburg and Mondrian, Neoplasticism principles, composition description, and the "asymmetric balance" significance sentence).
